newsitem.title: CANADA: Half of NW Prairie canola, wheat still unharvested.
newsitem.headline: Half of NW Prairie canola, wheat still unharvested.

text.p: Half of the canola and wheat grown in Alberta's Peace River Valley was yet to be combined as of Monday, Alberta and federal agriculture officials said.

"Nothing came off this weekend, it was really wet and snowy. It's snowing as we speak and there's no warming trend until the end of the week," Alberta Agriculture crop statistician Wendy Boje said in a phone interview.

About 900,000 acres in Alberta's Peace River Valley were seeded to canola, representing about 28 percent of provincial production. Half of that area was not harvested. Average canola yields ranged from 22 to 23 bushels an acre, Boje said.
Half of the Peace River Valley's 1.1 million wheat acres had also yet to be combined by Monday as well, Boje added.
That total area represents 15 percent of Alberta's wheat crop and average yields ranged from 33 to 34 bushels per acre.
Based on those acreage and yield forecasts, 493,958 tonnes of wheat and 224,530 tonnes of canola had yet to be harvested.
Ten cm (four inches) of snow fell on many parts of the Peace River Valley during the weekend, Boje said.
Alberta Agriculture's assessement of the harvest situation appeared reasonable, Agriculture Canada production analyst Gordon Reichart said.
The author of Alberta Wheat Pool's crop report, however, said harvest may be slightly higher.

Harvest of all crops in the Peace River Valley as of Oct 22 stood at 56 percent complete, with 75 percent of crops in the bin in Alberta's northern Peace, 51 percent in the south Peace and 35 percent combined in British Columbia's Peace, AWP's Joan Meants said in an interview.

Statistics Canada on Oct 8 set Prairie canola output at 4.979 million tonnes, down from last year's production of 6.436 million tonnes. Wheat output Canada-wide was forecast at 29.859 million tonnes, above last year's production of 25.037.
